panels.title: Treasury
panels.description: Latest credit balance on the newest transaction for the current era's player. Moves on every operation, not just trading.

panels.title: Trade Net (realised)
panels.description: Cargo sales minus cargo purchases for operation_type='tour' inside the selected window. Realised only: cargo still in a hold has been paid for but not yet sold, so this understates mid-run. See 'Capital in Cargo' beside it.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS "trade net"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Trade Revenue
panels.description: Gross credits received from SELL_CARGO on tour operations in the window.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0) AS "revenue"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Trade Spend
panels.description: Gross credits paid for PURCHASE_CARGO on tour operations in the window.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0) AS "spend"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Gross Margin
panels.description: Realised trade net as a percentage of cargo spend in the window. NULL-safe: shows the empty-state string rather than dividing by zero when nothing was bought.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)
             / NULLIF(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0), 1) AS "margin"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Realised Net / Hour
panels.description: Trade net divided by the length of the selected window, so 30m / 2h / 24h are comparable. Rate over the window, not an instantaneous reading.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)
       / NULLIF(EXTRACT(epoch FROM ($__timeTo()::timestamptz - $__timeFrom()::timestamptz)) / 3600.0, 0))::bigint
       AS "net per hour"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Trade Hulls
panels.description: Ships whose dedicated_fleet is 'trade' right now. Live fleet state, not filtered by the time window.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COUNT(*)::bigint AS "trade hulls"
  FROM ships s CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE s.player_id = me.pid AND s.dedicated_fleet = 'trade';

panels.title: Capital in Cargo (at cost)
panels.description: Credits spent in this window on cargo that has not been sold yet, valued at purchase price (no profit assumed). This is the counterweight to a negative realised net: money that is deployed, not lost.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
tx AS (SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull,
              MAX(t.created_at) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO') AS last_sell
         FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
        WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> '' AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
        GROUP BY 1)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount), 0) AS "in cargo"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
  LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.hull = t.metadata->>'ship_symbol'
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
   AND t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'
   AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
   AND t.created_at > COALESCE(tx.last_sell, $__timeFrom()::timestamptz);

panels.title: Best Hull
panels.description: Highest realised net in the window. Credits are pre-formatted server-side with to_char comma grouping because the field is a string, not a number.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
tx AS (SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull, COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS net
         FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
        WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> '' AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
        GROUP BY 1)
SELECT COALESCE((SELECT hull || '   ' || to_char(net, 'FM999G999G999') || ' CR'
                   FROM tx ORDER BY net DESC LIMIT 1), 'no hull traded in window') AS "best hull";

panels.title: Worst Hull
panels.description: Lowest realised net in the window. A MID-RUN hull can appear here purely because it has bought and not yet sold -- cross-check 'Net @ Cost' in the table below before reading it as a loss.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
tx AS (SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull, COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS net
         FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
        WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> '' AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
        GROUP BY 1)
SELECT COALESCE((SELECT hull || '   ' || to_char(net, 'FM999G999G999') || ' CR'
                   FROM tx ORDER BY net ASC LIMIT 1), 'no hull traded in window') AS "worst hull";

panels.title: Contract Net (all ops)
panels.description: Net credits across every contract transaction in the window: advances plus payouts minus cargo and fuel. Kept separate from trade because CONTRACT_FULFILLED carries no ship_symbol and cannot be attributed to a hull.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS "contract net"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'contract'
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Per-Hull P&L - realised, deployed, and honest net
panels.description:
The centrepiece. One row per hull in the trade fleet, plus any hull that traded in the window and has since been released. Scoped to operation_type='tour'.

**Realised Net** = sells - buys settled in the window. **In Cargo** is what the hull has paid for and not yet sold, at purchase price. **Net @ Cost** = Realised Net + In Cargo, which is the honest position of a hull caught mid-run: a freshly-bought hull reads ~0 there, not a loss. **Margin %** is blank until the hull has actually sold something.

Money columns honour the time picker. **State, Hold, Cap, System, Nav and Tour are live fleet state** - the `ships` table keeps no history, so those columns read 'now' even when the window is historical.

**State** reads the hull's assignment, not only its trades: TRADING = sold in this window; MID-RUN = holding cargo it has paid for; ON TOUR = claimed on a live tour that has not reached its first buy leg yet (planning, repositioning, refuelling) - working, not idle; IDLE = in the trade fleet with no tour, no cargo and no trades; RELEASED = traded in the window but has since left the trade fleet.

defaults.noValue: No trade-fleet hulls and no tour cargo transactions in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
tx AS (
  SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO')            AS buys,
         COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0) AS spent,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO')                AS sells,
         COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0)      AS earned,
         COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)                                               AS net,
         MAX(t.created_at) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO')       AS last_sell
    FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
   WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
     AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
   GROUP BY 1),
open_cargo AS (
  SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull, COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount), 0) AS open_cost
    FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
    LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.hull = t.metadata->>'ship_symbol'
   WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
     AND t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
     AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
     AND t.created_at > COALESCE(tx.last_sell, $__timeFrom()::timestamptz)
   GROUP BY 1),
fleet AS (SELECT s.* FROM ships s CROSS JOIN me
           WHERE s.player_id = me.pid AND s.dedicated_fleet = 'trade')
SELECT COALESCE(f.ship_symbol, tx.hull)                              AS "Hull",
       CASE WHEN f.ship_symbol IS NULL              THEN 'RELEASED'
            WHEN COALESCE(tx.sells,0) > 0           THEN 'TRADING'
            WHEN COALESCE(f.cargo_units,0) > 0      THEN 'MID-RUN'
            WHEN COALESCE(tx.buys,0)  > 0           THEN 'MID-RUN'
            WHEN COALESCE(f.assignment_status,'') = 'active'
             AND COALESCE(f.container_id,'') LIKE 'tour-run-%'
                                                    THEN 'ON TOUR'
            ELSE 'IDLE' END                                          AS "State",
       COALESCE(tx.buys, 0)                                          AS "Buys",
       COALESCE(tx.sells, 0)                                         AS "Sells",
       COALESCE(tx.spent, 0)                                         AS "Spent",
       COALESCE(tx.earned, 0)                                        AS "Earned",
       COALESCE(tx.net, 0)                                           AS "Realised Net",
       COALESCE(oc.open_cost, 0)                                     AS "In Cargo",
       COALESCE(tx.net, 0) + COALESCE(oc.open_cost, 0)               AS "Net @ Cost",
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(tx.sells,0) > 0 AND COALESCE(tx.spent,0) > 0
            THEN ROUND(100.0 * tx.net / tx.spent, 1) END             AS "Margin %",
       COALESCE(f.cargo_units, 0)                                    AS "Hold",
       COALESCE(f.cargo_capacity, 0)                                 AS "Cap",
       COALESCE(f.system_symbol, '-')                                AS "System",
       COALESCE(f.nav_status, '-')                                   AS "Nav",
       COALESCE(substring(f.container_id from '[0-9a-f]{8}$'), '-') AS "Tour"
  FROM tx
  FULL OUTER JOIN fleet f ON f.ship_symbol = tx.hull
  LEFT JOIN open_cargo oc ON oc.hull = COALESCE(f.ship_symbol, tx.hull)
 ORDER BY COALESCE(tx.net, 0) DESC;

panels.title: Realised Net by Hull
panels.description: Realised tour net per hull over the window, worst to best. Bars below zero are hulls that have bought and not yet sold -- compare with 'Net @ Cost' above before calling them unprofitable.

defaults.noValue: No hull traded on a tour in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS "Hull", COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS "Realised Net"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 ASC;

panels.title: Cumulative Net by Hull
panels.description: Running realised net per hull across the window. A flat line is a hull in transit or loading; a step up is a sale landing. Divergence between lines is the per-hull spread the fleet is actually earning.

defaults.noValue: No hull traded on a tour in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
b AS (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(t.created_at, $__interval),
             t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS metric,
             COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS v
        FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
       WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
         AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
       GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT time, metric, SUM(v) OVER (PARTITION BY metric ORDER BY time) AS value
  FROM b ORDER BY 1, 2;

panels.title: Revenue vs Spend vs Net
panels.description: Tour cargo flow bucketed by the dashboard interval. Spend is plotted positive so the two gross flows are directly comparable; Net is the signed difference.

defaults.noValue: No tour cargo transactions in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(t.created_at, $__interval),
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0)      AS "Revenue",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0) AS "Spend",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)                                                       AS "Net"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Cumulative Trade Net vs Treasury
panels.description: Cumulative realised trade net in the window against the actual credit balance. The gap between them is everything trading does not control -- ship purchases above all. If trade net climbs while treasury falls, capex is outspending the trade engine.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
spine AS (
  SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(t.created_at, $__interval),
         COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (
             WHERE t.operation_type = 'tour'
               AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
               AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''), 0) AS trade_v,
         (array_agg(t.balance_after ORDER BY t.created_at DESC))[1]   AS treasury
    FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
   WHERE t.player_id = me.pid
     AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
   GROUP BY 1)
SELECT time,
       SUM(trade_v) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS "Cumulative Trade Net",
       treasury                          AS "Treasury"
  FROM spine ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Hull payback  (LIFETIME - this whole section ignores the time picker)
Trade-Hull Capex (actual)
panels.description:
**LIFETIME - this panel deliberately ignores the dashboard time picker.** Payback is a cumulative quantity, so no `$__timeFilter` appears anywhere in its query; it reads the whole of the current era. A windowed version would show a hull older than the window earning only its last few hours and looking permanently unpaid, while still rendering a believable number.

Every credit spent on `PURCHASE_SHIP` for a trade-capable hull type (`SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER`, `SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER`) in the current era.

**This one needs no attribution at all** - it is a plain ledger sum, exact. It counts hulls that have since left the trade fleet or been lost, because the money was still spent. Probes, the command frigate and the explorer are excluded.

It is therefore *larger* than the sum of the *Capex* column in the per-hull table below, which covers only the hulls in the trade fleet right now.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount), 0) AS "trade-hull capex"
  FROM transactions t
 WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_SHIP'
   AND t.metadata->>'ship_type' IN ('SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER','SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER');

panels.title: Trade Net (lifetime, all hulls)
panels.description:
**LIFETIME - this panel deliberately ignores the dashboard time picker.** Payback is a cumulative quantity, so no `$__timeFilter` appears anywhere in its query; it reads the whole of the current era. A windowed version would show a hull older than the window earning only its last few hours and looking permanently unpaid, while still rendering a believable number.

Realised `operation_type='tour'` cargo net - sells minus buys - for every hull in the current era, including the hulls that have since left the fleet. Plain ledger sum, exact.

Cargo sitting in a hold right now is **not** credited here, so this is a conservative floor. The per-hull table's *Net @ Cost* column adds it back at purchase price.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS "lifetime trade net"
  FROM transactions t
 WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
   AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
   AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> '';

panels.title: Fleet Payback %
panels.description:
**LIFETIME - this panel deliberately ignores the dashboard time picker.** Payback is a cumulative quantity, so no `$__timeFilter` appears anywhere in its query; it reads the whole of the current era. A windowed version would show a hull older than the window earning only its last few hours and looking permanently unpaid, while still rendering a believable number.

Lifetime realised tour net divided by lifetime trade-hull capex, both straight from the ledger for the current era. **100% means trading has earned back every credit ever spent on trade hulls.**

This is the only payback figure on the dashboard that needs no capex attribution: both sides are exact sums over `transactions`, with no averaging and no per-hull join. Open cargo is left out of the numerator, so it reads slightly low.

targets.rawSql:
WITH cap AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount), 0) AS v
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_SHIP'
     AND t.metadata->>'ship_type' IN ('SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER','SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER')),
net AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS v
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
     AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> '')
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * net.v / NULLIF(cap.v, 0), 1) AS "fleet payback"
  FROM cap, net;

panels.title: Trade Fleet Paid Back
panels.description:
**LIFETIME - this panel deliberately ignores the dashboard time picker.** Payback is a cumulative quantity, so no `$__timeFilter` appears anywhere in its query; it reads the whole of the current era. A windowed version would show a hull older than the window earning only its last few hours and looking permanently unpaid, while still rendering a believable number.

How many hulls currently in `dedicated_fleet='trade'` have had their cumulative realised tour net cross their attributed purchase price at least once, out of the whole live trade fleet. A hull bought minutes ago counts in the denominator as not-paid-back - that is the point.

**Capex is a frame-class average, not this hull's actual receipt.** A `PURCHASE_SHIP` row stores `metadata->>'ship_symbol'` as the ship *type* (`SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER`), never the hull, and leaves `related_entity_type`/`related_entity_id` empty - so no purchase can be joined to the hull it produced. Each hull is therefore charged the mean `PURCHASE_SHIP` price for its frame in this era. Prices move: individual purchases spread roughly +/-10% around that mean (this era: -10% to +14%), which shifts a hull's payback by well under an hour at current rates. Treat capex as a class figure, never as per-hull precision.

**Hulls that traded earlier this era and have since left the fleet are excluded.** `ships` keeps no history, so a departed hull has no frame, and with no frame there is no capex to compare against. Their earnings *are* counted in *Trade Net (lifetime, all hulls)* and *Fleet Payback %* above.

targets.rawSql:
WITH capex AS (
  SELECT CASE t.metadata->>'ship_type'
           WHEN 'SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER' THEN 'FRAME_HEAVY_FREIGHTER'
           WHEN 'SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER'    THEN 'FRAME_LIGHT_FREIGHTER'
           WHEN 'SHIP_PROBE'           THEN 'FRAME_PROBE'
           WHEN 'SHIP_EXPLORER'        THEN 'FRAME_EXPLORER'
           WHEN 'SHIP_COMMAND_FRIGATE' THEN 'FRAME_FRIGATE'
         END                                                          AS frame,
         ROUND(AVG(-t.amount))::bigint                                AS avg_price
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_SHIP'
   GROUP BY 1),
tx AS (
  SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol'                                       AS hull,
         MIN(t.created_at)                                                AS first_trade,
         MAX(t.created_at) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type='SELL_CARGO') AS last_sell,
         COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)                                       AS net,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO')        AS sells
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
     AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   GROUP BY 1),
open_cargo AS (
  SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull, COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount), 0) AS open_cost
    FROM transactions t
    LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.hull = t.metadata->>'ship_symbol'
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
     AND t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
     AND t.created_at > COALESCE(tx.last_sell, '-infinity'::timestamptz)
   GROUP BY 1),
base AS (
  SELECT s.ship_symbol                                                 AS hull,
         s.frame_symbol,
         c.avg_price                                                   AS capex,
         tx.first_trade,
         COALESCE(tx.sells, 0)                                         AS sells,
         COALESCE(tx.net, 0)                                           AS realised,
         COALESCE(oc.open_cost, 0)                                     AS in_cargo,
         COALESCE(tx.net, 0) + COALESCE(oc.open_cost, 0)               AS at_cost,
         (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - tx.first_trade)) / 3600.0)::numeric AS tenure_h
    FROM ships s
    LEFT JOIN capex c       ON c.frame = s.frame_symbol
    LEFT JOIN tx            ON tx.hull = s.ship_symbol
    LEFT JOIN open_cargo oc ON oc.hull = s.ship_symbol
   WHERE s.player_id = $player AND s.dedicated_fleet = 'trade'),
running AS (
  SELECT t.metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull, t.created_at,
         SUM(t.amount) OVER (PARTITION BY t.metadata->>'ship_symbol'
                             ORDER BY t.created_at, t.id) AS cum
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
     AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''),
paid AS (
  SELECT r.hull, MIN(r.created_at) AS paid_at
    FROM running r JOIN base b ON b.hull = r.hull
   WHERE b.capex IS NOT NULL AND r.cum >= b.capex
   GROUP BY 1),
h AS (
  SELECT b.*, p.paid_at,
         (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p.paid_at - b.first_trade)) / 3600.0)::numeric AS paid_h,
         b.at_cost / NULLIF(b.tenure_h, 0)                                   AS rate
    FROM base b LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.hull = b.hull)
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE paid_at IS NOT NULL)::text
       || ' / ' || COUNT(*)::text || ' hulls' AS "paid back"
  FROM h;

panels.title: Median Payback Time
panels.description:
**LIFETIME - this panel deliberately ignores the dashboard time picker.** Payback is a cumulative quantity, so no `$__timeFilter` appears anywhere in its query; it reads the whole of the current era. A windowed version would show a hull older than the window earning only its last few hours and looking permanently unpaid, while still rendering a believable number.

Median hours from a hull's first tour trade to the moment its cumulative realised net first covered its attributed capex.

**Right-censored on purpose.** Only hulls that HAVE paid back are in the sample. Hulls still working towards it are excluded rather than counted as slow, because they do not yet have a payback time to count. That biases this figure low - the fast hulls enter the sample first - so always read it next to *Trade Fleet Paid Back*, which gives you the denominator. A mean over all hulls would be meaningless for exactly this reason and is not shown.

Frames are mixed: a light hauler costs about a fifth of a heavy and pays back sooner, so the figure drifts with fleet composition. The per-hull table carries the frame per row.

Measured from first trade, not from purchase - there is no per-hull purchase timestamp for the same reason there is no per-hull price. On this era's hulls the gap between buying a hull and its first trade ran 2 to 75 minutes, so true payback from purchase is that much longer.

targets.rawSql:
WITH capex AS (
  SELECT CASE t.metadata->>'ship_type'

panels.title: Per-Hull Payback - how long each hull takes to earn back its price
panels.description:
**LIFETIME - this panel deliberately ignores the dashboard time picker.** Payback is a cumulative quantity, so no `$__timeFilter` appears anywhere in its query; it reads the whole of the current era. A windowed version would show a hull older than the window earning only its last few hours and looking permanently unpaid, while still rendering a believable number.

One row per hull in the trade fleet right now, ordered **worst-remaining first** - the actionable end. Hulls that have paid back sink to the bottom.

**Capex is a frame-class average, not this hull's actual receipt.** A `PURCHASE_SHIP` row stores `metadata->>'ship_symbol'` as the ship *type* (`SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER`), never the hull, and leaves `related_entity_type`/`related_entity_id` empty - so no purchase can be joined to the hull it produced. Each hull is therefore charged the mean `PURCHASE_SHIP` price for its frame in this era. Prices move: individual purchases spread roughly +/-10% around that mean (this era: -10% to +14%), which shifts a hull's payback by well under an hour at current rates. Treat capex as a class figure, never as per-hull precision.

**Tenure** is hours since the hull's *first tour trade*, not since purchase: no per-hull purchase timestamp exists either. On this era's hulls the purchase-to-first-trade gap ran 2 to 75 minutes, so every payback figure here is optimistic by roughly that much. Blank tenure means the hull has never traded.

**Payback %, Net @ Cost / h and ETA are all computed on Net @ Cost**, matching the *Per-Hull P&L* table above: `Realised Net + In Cargo`, where *In Cargo* is what the hull has paid for and not yet sold, valued at purchase price. Without that, a hull that has just loaded a full hold reads as a large loss and its payback goes negative - a wrong number that looks entirely plausible. *In Cargo* is a cost floor, not a mark-to-market: no profit is assumed on it.

**Paid back in** is measured differently on purpose: it is the first moment the hull's *realised* cumulative net crossed capex, i.e. when it had actually banked its price. So a hull can read PAID while its current *Payback %* has dipped back under 100 - it crossed, then spent cash on another load. That is a real distinction, not an inconsistency.

**ETA** is the remaining gap divided by the hull's own observed Net @ Cost per hour. It is blank whenever that rate is zero or negative, because extrapolating a negative rate produces a negative time-to-payback, which is nonsense. Blank means "cannot be projected yet", not zero.

*Tenure*, *Paid back in* and *ETA* are durations and auto-scale their own unit - the same column will read `6.41 hour` on one row and `2.05 days` on another.

**Status**: PAID = realised net crossed capex. PAID @ COST = the current position covers capex but it has not been banked yet. NO TRADES = bought, never traded, full capex outstanding. NO SALES YET = has bought a load but not completed a sale, so there is no margin to project from. EARNING = working towards it. STALLED = has sold, but its Net @ Cost rate is no longer positive. NO CAPEX = the hull's frame has no `PURCHASE_SHIP` history in this era, so nothing can be attributed to it.

Every query in this section filters `COALESCE(metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''`, so the empty-string `ship_symbol` that `REFUEL` rows carry cannot manufacture a phantom blank hull.

    FROM transactions t

     AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''

    FROM transactions t

    LEFT JOIN tx            ON tx.hull = s.ship_symbol

   WHERE s.player_id = $player AND s.dedicated_fleet = 'trade'),
running AS (

                             ORDER BY t.created_at, t.id) AS cum
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
     AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
     AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''),
paid AS (
  SELECT r.hull, MIN(r.created_at) AS paid_at
    FROM running r JOIN base b ON b.hull = r.hull
   WHERE b.capex IS NOT NULL AND r.cum >= b.capex
   GROUP BY 1),
h AS (
  SELECT b.*, p.paid_at,
         (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p.paid_at - b.first_trade)) / 3600.0)::numeric AS paid_h,
         b.at_cost / NULLIF(b.tenure_h, 0)                                   AS rate
    FROM base b LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.hull = b.hull)
SELECT h.hull                                            AS "Hull",
       replace(h.frame_symbol, 'FRAME_', '')             AS "Frame",
       ROUND(h.tenure_h, 2)                              AS "Tenure",
       h.capex                                           AS "Capex (frame avg)",
       h.realised                                        AS "Realised Net",
       h.in_cargo                                        AS "In Cargo",
       h.at_cost                                         AS "Net @ Cost",
       ROUND(h.rate)                                     AS "Net @ Cost / h",
       CASE WHEN h.capex > 0
            THEN ROUND(100.0 * h.at_cost / h.capex, 1) END AS "Payback %",
       ROUND(h.paid_h, 2)                                AS "Paid back in",
       CASE WHEN h.paid_at IS NULL AND h.capex IS NOT NULL AND h.rate > 0
            THEN ROUND((h.capex - h.at_cost) / h.rate, 2) END AS "ETA",
       CASE WHEN h.paid_at IS NOT NULL THEN 0

  FROM h
 ORDER BY CASE WHEN h.paid_at IS NOT NULL THEN 0
               ELSE GREATEST(COALESCE(h.capex, 0) - h.at_cost, 0) END DESC,

panels.title: Fleet Cumulative Trade Net vs Trade-Hull Capex
panels.description:
**LIFETIME on a fixed 7-day axis** - this panel overrides the dashboard time picker (`Last 7 days`, shown in its header) because a cumulative curve clipped to a short window starts from zero mid-history and reads as if nothing had been earned.

Both running sums are deliberately computed over the **whole era** and the query applies no time filter of its own: the axis clips what you see, the maths never does. Narrow the override and the curves keep their true levels instead of restarting at zero. The only bound is `player_id`, which scopes it to the current era.

**Green** is cumulative realised tour net across every hull. **Amber** is cumulative `PURCHASE_SHIP` outlay on trade-capable hull types, which steps up each time a hull is bought. Where green crosses above amber, the trading fleet has paid for itself; the gap afterwards is profit on hull capital. Each amber step is a fresh hull pushing the bar back up - a rising amber line with a flat green one is the shape to worry about.

**No capex attribution is involved here.** Both series are plain ledger sums, so this is the most trustworthy payback view on the dashboard - it just cannot tell you *which* hull is carrying the fleet. Open cargo is excluded, so green sits slightly low.

defaults.noValue: No transactions in the current era

targets.rawSql:
WITH ev AS (
  SELECT t.created_at,
         CASE WHEN t.operation_type = 'tour'
               AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
               AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
              THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END AS trade_v,
         CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_SHIP'
               AND t.metadata->>'ship_type' IN ('SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER','SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER')
              THEN -t.amount ELSE 0 END AS capex_v
    FROM transactions t
   WHERE t.player_id = $player),
b AS (
  SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, $__interval),
         COALESCE(SUM(trade_v), 0) AS trade_v,
         COALESCE(SUM(capex_v), 0) AS capex_v
    FROM ev
   GROUP BY 1),
c AS (
  SELECT time,
         SUM(trade_v) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS net,
         SUM(capex_v) OVER (ORDER BY time) AS capex
    FROM b)
-- Deliberately unfiltered by time.  Both series must carry their true cumulative
-- level at the left edge of whatever window is shown, so the running sums span the
-- whole era and the panel axis does the clipping.  A time macro on the grouped
-- column would not work here anyway: it is an epoch number, not a timestamptz.
SELECT time,
       net   AS "Cumulative Trade Net",
       capex AS "Cumulative Trade-Hull Capex"
  FROM c
 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Profitability by Good
panels.description: Tour cargo grouped by good. Net is meaningful here because a good is bought and sold as the same commodity -- but it is still window-clipped: a good sold in this window from cargo bought before it shows revenue with no matching spend, and vice versa.

defaults.noValue: No tour cargo transactions in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(t.metadata->>'good_symbol',''), '(unknown)')                      AS "Good",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0)  AS "Spent",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0)       AS "Earned",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)                                                        AS "Net",
       COALESCE(SUM((t.metadata->>'units')::bigint)
                FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0)                     AS "Units Sold",
       CASE WHEN SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO') > 0
            THEN ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.amount)
                 / SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 1) END AS "Margin %"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 4 DESC;

panels.title: Buy-side vs Sell-side by System
panels.description: Where cargo is sourced and where it is vended, by the system owning each transaction waypoint. **There is deliberately no net column here**: goods are bought in one system and sold in another, so a per-system net would be an artefact of the route, not a profit or a loss. 'Flow' is sell-side minus buy-side volume, i.e. whether a system is a source or a sink.

defaults.noValue: No tour cargo transactions in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(w.system_symbol, '(unmapped waypoint)')                                 AS "System",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0) AS "Bought Here",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0)      AS "Sold Here",
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO')                    AS "Buys",
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO')                        AS "Sells",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'SELL_CARGO'), 0)
       - COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0) AS "Flow"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
  LEFT JOIN waypoints w ON w.waypoint_symbol = t.metadata->>'waypoint'
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'tour'
       AND t.transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
       AND COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> ''
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC;

panels.title: Realised Capital by Operation
panels.description: Every transaction in the window grouped by operation_type -- the honest answer to 'why did treasury move'. Trading can be strongly positive while the balance falls, because 'fleet expansion' (ship purchases) is capex booked in the same ledger.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(t.operation_type,''), '(unattributed)')      AS "Operation",
       COUNT(*)                                                     AS "Txns",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.amount < 0), 0)      AS "Outflow",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.amount > 0), 0)       AS "Inflow",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)                                   AS "Net"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 5 DESC;

panels.title: Cumulative Net by Operation
panels.description: Running net per operation_type. The downward line is almost always 'fleet expansion': capex, not a trading loss.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players),
b AS (SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(t.created_at, $__interval),
             COALESCE(NULLIF(t.operation_type,''), '(unattributed)') AS metric,
             COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS v
        FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
       WHERE t.player_id = me.pid
         AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
       GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT time, metric, SUM(v) OVER (PARTITION BY metric ORDER BY time) AS value
  FROM b ORDER BY 1, 2;

panels.title: Contract Economics (fleet level - not attributable per hull)
panels.description: Contract money in full. CONTRACT_ACCEPTED is the advance, CONTRACT_FULFILLED the payout; **neither carries a ship_symbol**, so contract revenue can never be split per hull. The cargo and fuel costs below *are* per-hull attributable, which is exactly why a naive per-hull net would show every contract hull deeply negative. That is why the P&L table above is scoped to tours.

defaults.noValue: No contract activity in this window

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'CONTRACT_ACCEPTED'), 0)  AS "Advances",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'CONTRACT_FULFILLED'), 0) AS "Payouts",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'PURCHASE_CARGO'), 0)    AS "Cargo Cost",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (WHERE t.transaction_type = 'REFUEL'), 0)            AS "Fuel",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0)                                                          AS "Net"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.operation_type = 'contract'
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at);

panels.title: Fuel by Operation (fleet level only)
panels.description: Refuelling spend per operation. REFUEL rows store ship_symbol as an **empty string**, so fuel cannot be attributed to a hull -- it is deliberately absent from the per-hull table rather than guessed at.

targets.rawSql:
WITH me AS (SELECT MAX(id) AS pid FROM players)
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(t.operation_type,''), '(unattributed)') AS "Operation",
       COUNT(*)                                                AS "Refuels",
       COALESCE(SUM(-t.amount), 0)                             AS "Fuel Spend",
       COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(-t.amount)), 0)::bigint              AS "Avg per Refuel"
  FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN me
 WHERE t.player_id = me.pid AND t.transaction_type = 'REFUEL'
   AND $__timeFilter(t.created_at)
 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC;

panels.title: What this dashboard cannot show you (attribution limits)

options.content:
Five limits are structural in the `transactions` ledger. Nothing here infers around them, because a fabricated number is worse than an absent one.

**Contract revenue has no hull.** `CONTRACT_ACCEPTED` and `CONTRACT_FULFILLED` carry no `ship_symbol` in their metadata - only `contract_id` and `faction`. Their cargo purchases *do* carry one. Any per-hull net spanning both would show every contract hull deeply negative, so the P&L table is scoped to `operation_type='tour'` and contract money is reported whole, at fleet level, in *Contract Economics*. Contract hulls are correctly absent from the per-hull table, not hidden.

**Fuel has no hull.** Every `REFUEL` row stores `ship_symbol` as an **empty string**, not null - so the usual `IS NOT NULL` guard lets them through and silently creates a phantom blank-named hull that absorbs all fuel spend. Every query here filters on `<> ''` instead. Fuel is therefore shown per operation only, and per-hull net is *before* fuel.

**Held cargo has no cost basis.** `ships.cargo_inventory` records goods and units but no purchase price. *In Cargo* is reconstructed from purchases made after a hull's last sale inside the window, valued at cost with no profit assumed. It is a sound floor, not a mark-to-market: a hull that bought before the window opened contributes nothing to it.

**A hull purchase has no hull.** A `PURCHASE_SHIP` row stores `metadata->>'ship_symbol'` as the ship *type* - `SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER`, not `TORWIND-142` - puts the same string in `transaction_id`, and leaves `related_entity_type` and `related_entity_id` empty. No purchase can be joined to the hull it produced, and `ships` carries no purchase price or purchase timestamp either. The *Hull payback* section therefore charges each hull the mean price for its frame in this era and says so on every panel. Fleet-level payback avoids the problem entirely by summing both sides of the ledger. Fixing it properly means recording the real ship symbol at purchase time, which would only help hulls bought after the change.

**The window clips open positions at both ends.** A sale settling just inside the window from cargo bought just outside it shows revenue with no matching spend, inflating both margin and net; the mirror case deflates them. Widen the range until the figures stop moving before drawing a conclusion from a short window.

*Per-tour planned-vs-actual profit is not modelled here at all - the tour planner's expected margin is not persisted alongside the realised transactions. `SpaceTraders - Heavy Trading` (uid `spacetraders-trading`) carries the tour-lifecycle and guard diagnostics; this dashboard is deliberately the P&L view and does not duplicate it.*
